Fatal Runway Overshoot Leads Amazon to Suspend 21 Air Operations
Inside the Miami Plane Crash That Led Amazon to Halt Carrier Partnership
spot: Amazon has suspended its operations with cargo carrier 21 Air following a tragic incident on September 6, 2026, where one of the carrier's Boeing 767 planes overshot a runway at Miami International Airport, resulting in the deaths of five people and injuries to five others. The decision, announced Sunday, comes as investigators continue to probe the cause of the fatal crash.
content_html:
Key Developments

Amazon announced its decision to pause operations with 21 Air, the operator of Flight 7598, after a Boeing 767 cargo plane overshot a runway at Miami International Airport on September 6. The incident tragically killed five individuals who were in a van struck by the aircraft, and injured five others. Amazon spokesperson Kelly Nantel stated that the company spent time supporting the investigation and reviewing circumstances before making the decision, emphasizing that "Safety has always been our top priority."

The North Carolina-based carrier had been flying packages for Amazon since 2024. The fatal crash involved a 32-year-old Boeing 767, which was originally built for passenger transport and flew for various international airlines for over two decades before its conversion to a cargo plane in 2015.

Investigators from the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) are currently examining several factors, including the jet's ownership history, prevailing weather conditions at the airport, maintenance records, and 21 Air's operational procedures. Flight information released by the NTSB on September 9 revealed critical details from the cockpit audio recordings. One pilot reportedly warned their counterpart about excessive speed during the approach and after touchdown. The recordings also captured automated warnings from the aircraft regarding the speed of descent and approaching terrain. The full transcript of the cockpit conversation is expected to be released later in the investigation.

Key Takeaways

  • Amazon has suspended its partnership with 21 Air following a fatal runway overshoot incident at Miami International Airport on September 6, which killed five people.
  • The tragic crash involved a 21 Air Boeing 767 cargo plane that overshot the runway by approximately 1,300 feet, colliding with a van carrying airport workers.
  • NTSB investigators are reviewing multiple factors, including cockpit audio that indicated pilot warnings about excessive speed during the landing approach.

Why It Matters

This incident highlights the critical importance of aviation safety protocols and operational oversight, especially for cargo carriers partnering with major global logistics companies like Amazon. The suspension by Amazon underscores a commitment to safety standards within its supply chain, potentially setting a precedent for how other e-commerce giants vet and manage their third-party logistics partners. The ongoing NTSB investigation into the crash, particularly the details emerging from cockpit recordings, will be crucial in understanding the contributing factors and could lead to significant changes in aviation safety regulations and pilot training for cargo operations. The tragic loss of life also brings renewed focus on ground safety measures at busy international airports.
